_comment: Random weekly nudges; the writer gets 2 per episode (seeded). Add, remove, or reword freely.
directives: Michael calls an unnecessary all-staff meeting that spirals out of control.
A Jim-and-Pam prank on Dwight escalates beyond what they planned.
A talking head flatly contradicts what we see in the very next scene.
Give a background character (Creed, Meredith, Kevin, Stanley or Phyllis) their own small B- or C-plot.
Someone from corporate visits, and everyone pretends to be a functional office.
Two unlikely characters are forced to work together and discover something in common.
Dwight sees a chance to seize power and goes too far.
Someone keeps a secret all episode, and it comes out at the worst moment.
A small office competition (a contest, a bet, a game) takes over the day.
Andy tries too hard to be liked and it backfires.
The episode leaves the office: a sales call, a client lunch, or an outing (use offsite).
Toby tries to enforce a rule and Michael makes it personal.
Angela and the Party Planning Committee clash over an upcoming event.
Pay off a running gag or storyline note from the story so far.
Plant the seed of something that will pay off in a later episode, without resolving it.
Michael attempts to do something genuinely kind, in the worst possible way.
A misunderstanding spreads through the office like a game of telephone.
Kevin has an unexpected moment of competence or wisdom.
The warehouse and the office clash, and Darryl is the voice of reason.
Someone gets a romantic subplot: a crush, a bad date, or a jealous moment.
Introduce or bring back a recurring extra (a client, a neighbor, a rival from another branch, a delivery person).
